Barbari Bread

Served at: Yalda Night

2 loavesPrep 2 hours (including rising time)Cook 20-25 min

Barbari bread is a beloved traditional Persian flatbread, distinguished by its elongated shape, crispy crust, and soft, airy interior. It is a staple at Yalda Night, the ancient Persian celebration of the winter solstice, where it's often served alongside feta cheese, fresh herbs, and the symbolic fruits of the longest night, like watermelon and pomegranates.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) warm water (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast
  • 1 teaspoon (4 g) granulated sugar
  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons (9 g) salt
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil, plus more for greasing
  • For the Roomal (Glaze):
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1 g) baking soda
  • For Topping:
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) sesame seeds (white, black, or a mix)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
  2. Add the 4 cups of flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
  3. Add the 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. The dough should be slightly sticky.
  4. Lightly grease a clean large bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  5. While the dough is rising, prepare the Roomal (glaze): In a small saucepan, whisk together the 1/4 cup flour, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, and baking soda until smooth. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a thin, gravy-like consistency. Remove from heat and let it cool completely.
  6. Once the dough has risen, gently punch it down and divide it into two equal pieces.
  7. On a piece of parchment paper (or a lightly floured surface), gently stretch and shape each piece of dough into an elongated oval or rectangular shape, about 12-14 inches (30-35 cm) long and 5-6 inches (12-15 cm) wide. Transfer the parchment paper with the dough to a baking sheet.
  8. Using your fingertips, gently press parallel indentations (ridges) along the length of each loaf, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart. Be careful not to press all the way through the dough.
  9. Cover the shaped loaves loosely with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let them rise again for 20-30 minutes, or until slightly puffy.
  10. Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C) with a baking stone or an inverted baking sheet inside, if you have one, for at least 30 minutes.
  11. Just before baking, generously brush the cooled Roomal glaze over the surface of each loaf, ensuring it gets into the indentations. Sprinkle evenly with sesame seeds.
  12. Carefully transfer the parchment paper with the loaves onto the preheated baking stone or baking sheet. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and crispy.
  13. Remove the bread from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For an extra crispy crust, place a shallow pan of hot water on the bottom rack of your oven during baking to create steam.
  • The Roomal glaze is key to Barbari's unique texture and shine; ensure it's cool before applying.
  • Barbari is best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven, with a spread of feta cheese and fresh herbs like mint and basil.
